title: Anticipation effects in DID: pre-announced policy

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences with explicit anticipation window plus an event-study check.
- Why: The policy was announced in period 3 but implemented in period 5. A standard DID with a single post dummy would be biased if treated banks adjust upon announcement. Including two interactions lets us separately identify:
  - Anticipation effect in announcement window (periods 3–4): treated × announce
  - Additional implementation effect from period 5 onward: treated × post
- Estimating equation (TWFE):
  y_it = α_i + γ_t + β_A (treated_i × announce_t) + β_P (treated_i × post_t) + ε_it
  where announce_t = 1{t ≥ 3}, post_t = 1{t ≥ 5}.
  Interpretation: Effect in periods 3–4 is β_A; effect in periods ≥5 is β_A + β_P.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: Absent the policy, treated and control banks would have evolved similarly (verified using pre-announcement periods 1–2).
  - Anticipation is activated only by the public announcement (i.e., no other differential shocks hit treated banks at t=3–4).
  - Stable composition/SUTVA and no differential measurement error across groups.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Packages
pkgs <- c("data.table", "fixest")
for(p in pkgs){
  if(!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p)
}
library(data.table)
library(fixest)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s10_data.csv"
dt <- fread(path)

# 2) Construct policy timing variables
# Ensure integers
dt[, period := as.integer(period)]
dt[, treated := as.integer(treated)]

# Define announce (>=3) and post (>=5). If post exists, keep but ensure consistency.
dt[, announce := as.integer(period >= 3)]
if(!"post" %in% names(dt)) dt[, post := as.integer(period >= 5)] else dt[, post := as.integer(post)]

# Interactions (recompute to be safe)
dt[, treat_x_announce := treated * announce]
dt[, treat_x_post     := treated * post]

# 3) Baseline TWFE with anticipation and implementation effects
mod_main <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_announce + treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
  cluster = ~ unit_id, data = dt
)

# Extract coefficients, SEs, CIs
V <- vcov(mod_main)
bA <- coef(mod_main)["treat_x_announce"]
bP <- coef(mod_main)["treat_x_post"]
seA <- sqrt(V["treat_x_announce","treat_x_announce"])
seP <- sqrt(V["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"])

ciA <- bA + c(-1,1) * 1.96 * seA
ciP <- bP + c(-1,1) * 1.96 * seP

# Total post-implementation effect (anticipation + implementation increment)
bTot <- bA + bP
seTot <- sqrt(V["treat_x_announce","treat_x_announce"] +
              V["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"] +
              2*V["treat_x_announce","treat_x_post"])
ciTot <- bTot + c(-1,1) * 1.96 * seTot

# 4) Event-study around the announcement to assess pre-trends and dynamics
# Coefficients are deviations for treated vs control by period relative to period 2 (pre-announcement)
mod_es <- feols(
  y ~ i(period, treated, ref = 2) | unit_id + period,
  cluster = ~ unit_id, data = dt
)

# Extract pre-trend test (only period 1 is pre relative to ref=2)
es_coef <- coef(mod_es)
es_vcv  <- vcov(mod_es)

name_p1 <- "period::1#treated"
pre1_b  <- if(name_p1 %in% names(es_coef)) es_coef[name_p1] else NA_real_
pre1_se <- if(!is.na(pre1_b)) sqrt(es_vcv[name_p1, name_p1]) else NA_real_
pre1_t  <- if(!is.na(pre1_b) && pre1_se > 0) pre1_b / pre1_se else NA_real_
pre1_p  <- if(!is.na(pre1_t)) 2*pnorm(-abs(pre1_t)) else NA_real_

# 5) Robustness A: Estimate anticipation effect using only pre-implementation window (periods <=4)
dt_early <- dt[period <= 4]
mod_early <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_announce | unit_id + period,
  cluster = ~ unit_id, data = dt_early
)
bA_early <- coef(mod_early)["treat_x_announce"]
seA_early <- sqrt(vcov(mod_early)["treat_x_announce","treat_x_announce"])
ciA_early <- bA_early + c(-1,1) * 1.96 * seA_early

# 6) Robustness B: Placebo DID in periods 1–2 (fake "announcement" at period 2)
dt_placebo <- dt[period <= 2]
dt_placebo[, placebo_announce := as.integer(period >= 2)]
dt_placebo[, treat_x_placebo := treated * placebo_announce]
mod_placebo <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_placebo | unit_id + period,
  cluster = ~ unit_id, data = dt_placebo
)
b_placebo <- coef(mod_placebo)["treat_x_placebo"]
se_placebo <- sqrt(vcov(mod_placebo)["treat_x_placebo","treat_x_placebo"])
ci_placebo <- b_placebo + c(-1,1) * 1.96 * se_placebo

# 7) Robustness C: Add unit-specific linear trends
dt[, t := as.numeric(period)]
mod_trend <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_announce + treat_x_post | unit_id + period + unit_id^t,
  cluster = ~ unit_id, data = dt
)
bA_trend <- coef(mod_trend)["treat_x_announce"]
bP_trend <- coef(mod_trend)["treat_x_post"]

# 8) Print clear numerical results
cat("Baseline TWFE (unit and period FE, clustered SEs):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Anticipation effect (treated x announce, periods 3–4):  %.4f  (SE=%.4f)  95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            bA, seA, ciA[1], ciA[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Additional implementation effect (treated x post, >=5): %.4f  (SE=%.4f)  95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            bP, seP, ciP[1], ciP[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Total effect after implementation (>=5):               %.4f  (SE=%.4f)  95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n",
            bTot, seTot, ciTot[1], ciTot[2]))

cat("Event-study pre-trend check (relative to period 2):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Period 1 coefficient (treated vs control, vs t=2):    %.4f  (SE=%.4f)  p-value=%.4f\n\n",
            pre1_b, pre1_se, pre1_p))

cat("Robustness A (only periods <=4):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Anticipation effect (treated x announce):             %.4f  (SE=%.4f)  95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n",
            bA_early, seA_early, ciA_early[1], ciA_early[2]))

cat("Robustness B (placebo in periods 1–2; fake announce at t=2):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Placebo effect (treated x fake announce):             %.4f  (SE=%.4f)  95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n",
            b_placebo, se_placebo, ci_placebo[1], ci_placebo[2]))

cat("Robustness C (add unit-specific linear trends):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Anticipation (with trends):                           %.4f\n", bA_trend))
cat(sprintf("  Implementation increment (with trends):               %.4f\n", bP_trend))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Treated banks (below the threshold) should raise Tier-1 capital ratios in anticipation after the announcement (periods 3–4), and further upon implementation (period ≥5).
- Magnitude: Anticipation effect around 0.3–0.6 percentage points; additional implementation effect around 0.5–1.0 percentage points; total post-implementation effect roughly 0.8–1.6 p.p. If anticipation is strong, β_A will be statistically significant and nontrivial; if not, β_A ≈ 0 and the increase will load mainly on β_P. Pre-trend tests (period 1 vs 2) should be near zero and insignificant.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID with anticipation — must account for pre-announcement window; use period ≤2 as clean pre-period
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Constrained banks raise capital ratios both after announcement and after effective date
